config.question: What testable dispute-resolution methods emerge by transferring lessons among influential contested AI, psychology and economics papers?

display.title: Disagreement deserves better experiments.
display.description: Six high-attention disputes. Original claims, critiques and follow-ups stay attached while the mixer evolves testable ways to discriminate explanations.
display.sourceHeading: Six disputes. Evidence on more than one side.
display.nextDescription: Continue a dispute-resolution proposal with an explicit test, not a stronger rhetorical claim.

config.name: Controversial papers: dispute-resolution mixer
config.archiveRule: One eligible proposal per application-domain × dispute lever niche, highest mean AI-rated formulation score; strict ties retain incumbent. No score for controversy, citations, agreement or rhetorical force.
config.eligibility: Two distinct focal paper dossiers from at least two domains, each with locators and transfer boundaries. The target domain must be represented. Both critics accept the niche, flag no fatal scope distortion, and score grounding >=2. Preserve original, challenge and reply scope.
config.selection: Two actual model-generated initial proposals per predefined niche; one feedback-guided child per initial elite. Targeted initialization, not an unbiased diversity benchmark.
limitations: This is a curated high-attention selection, not a citation-ranked or exhaustive list. No current citation counts are asserted.
Controversy is not evidence of error, fraud or equal evidential support. Normative claims and empirical hypotheses require different treatment.
Mix methods of resolving disputes, not effect sizes, populations or the truth values of unrelated claims.
AI ratings assess proposal formulation; neither model consensus nor citation attention establishes scientific truth.
All generator, critic and revision contexts share one inherited model family; they are not independent model replications.
No proposed human-subject study, policy intervention, original-data reanalysis or model capability benchmark has been executed.
Scores across this corpus and the earlier ALife corpus are not calibrated for comparison.

papers.boundary: Benchmark capability does not automatically resolve ethical claims; this is not a single empirical claim that one task can falsify.
papers.status: Conceptual and normative dispute; assess each empirical or ethical claim separately.
papers.attention: The lead author documents extensive media coverage; selected for attention, not a verified citation rank.

candidates.title: An endpoint ledger for impressive demonstrations

sources.locator: §§1.1, 8, 10; early-model disclosure
sources.use: Separate task demonstrations from broad capability interpretation.
sources.boundary: A new frozen model cannot reproduce the unavailable early GPT-4 build.

sources.locator: Original hormone, risk and subjective endpoints; larger-sample replication and broader meta-analysis
sources.use: Transfer endpoint separation to AI evaluation.
sources.boundary: Neither effect sizes nor a verdict on posture transfer to AI.

candidates.mechanism: A fluent explanation, executable answer and successful transfer are different endpoints. Carry the endpoint distinctions emphasized by the power-posing dispute into a capability ledger so a persuasive narrative cannot substitute for correctness or robustness.
candidates.hypothesis: On a frozen local model, explanation fluency will show weaker agreement with held-out task correctness than executable checks do; an agreement gap below 0.10 would favor endpoint convergence over dissociation.
candidates.experiment: Preregister 60 procedurally generated logic/programming task families and four surface variants each. Freeze prompts, decoding and model checksum. Score exact solutions, executable tests, counterfactual transfer and a fixed textual-fluency rubric separately; bootstrap families, not variants.
candidates.baseline: Same 240 outputs, equal token budgets; compare an unweighted four-endpoint composite with the preregistered endpoint ledger. A generator provides hidden correct solutions. No evaluator sees task provenance.
candidates.metric: Family-level endpoint disagreement, correctness calibration, and the fluency-versus-executable agreement difference with bootstrap intervals.
candidates.falsifier: A narrow interval wholly below the 0.10 disagreement-gap threshold favors coherent endpoints; large preregistered dissociation favors reporting separate competencies.
candidates.confound: Rubric reliability and task difficulty can create apparent dissociation; retain raw scores and stratify by generator difficulty.
candidates.feasibility: Offline audit, 240 generations plus local tests; synthetic success does not establish general intelligence.

candidates.title: Cost denominators without a single understanding score

sources.locator: Environmental-cost, opportunity-cost and language-understanding discussions
sources.use: Keep empirical resource accounting separate from conceptual and ethical claims.
sources.boundary: A local energy proxy cannot settle historical training emissions or social value.

sources.locator: Debt-bin aggregation; critical replication on weighting and inclusion; author response
sources.use: Audit how denominators and group weighting alter a summary.
sources.boundary: No debt threshold, causal direction or economics effect transfers.

candidates.mechanism: Different denominators answer different questions. Transfer the debt dispute's aggregation audit to AI resource evaluation: cost per request, cost per verified answer and cost per task family can rank the same systems differently without resolving ethical judgments.
candidates.hypothesis: Two frozen local models' cost rankings will reverse across at least two preregistered denominators if one gains accuracy mainly on long tasks; stable rankings would favor denominator robustness.
candidates.experiment: Use 80 synthetic task families, balanced easy/hard and short/long. Record wall time and generated tokens for one fixed attempt per model; use measured joules only if a supported meter exists. Report four denominators and all task failures.
candidates.baseline: Identical hardware, task families and output caps; alternate execution order. Compare equal-family weighting with request weighting. Treat tokens/time as proxies explicitly, never as emissions.
candidates.metric: Rank reversals, resource per verified answer, failure-inclusive totals and family-bootstrap intervals.
candidates.falsifier: Consistent rankings with narrow paired uncertainty across all four denominators weaken denominator sensitivity; reversals support a conditional efficiency conclusion.
candidates.confound: Warm-up, caching and output length; freeze cache policy, randomize order, and report uncached/cached strata.
candidates.feasibility: 160 local generations; a resource-accounting proposal only. The Parrots normative concerns remain separate even if efficiency improves.

candidates.title: Synthetic natural experiments for evidence use

sources.locator: §7.2.1, §8 and §10 capability examples and limitations
sources.use: Turn selected task performance into a narrowly defined intervention test.
sources.boundary: No single benchmark identifies general intelligence or exactly repeats early GPT-4.

sources.locator: Original NJ/PA before-after comparison; 2000 comment and reply
sources.use: Transfer explicit comparison-group and measurement assumptions.
sources.boundary: A synthetic randomized intervention does not inherit wage-study effects or policy validity.

candidates.mechanism: An answer may follow supplied evidence or remembered associations. Transfer comparison-group scrutiny into a randomized synthetic evidence intervention: preserve task form while changing only a fictional rule, and compare changes against an untouched matched rule.
candidates.hypothesis: If answers use supplied rules, random rule reversals will shift the affected answers by at least 0.60 more than matched unaffected answers; generic prompt disruption predicts similar degradation in both.
candidates.experiment: Generate 100 fictional-world families with two independent rules and known answers. Randomly reverse one rule in half the families' paired prompts; retain unaltered companion questions. Freeze model, prompt template and scoring before collection.
candidates.baseline: Same families, token cap and query count for intervention and control. Estimate a paired difference in changes, with family as unit; include a neutral text-edit placebo of matched length.
candidates.metric: Difference-in-differences in rule-consistent answer probability, placebo degradation and family-randomization intervals.
candidates.falsifier: Near-zero targeted contrast with comparable affected/unaffected degradation favors disruption or shallow matching; a targeted contrast above 0.60 with low placebo effect favors evidence-sensitive behavior on these tasks.
candidates.confound: Rule ambiguity or changed tokenization; use balanced symbol assignments and deterministic ground-truth validation.
candidates.feasibility: Approximately 600 offline generations; intervention causality is confined to generated prompts and this frozen model.

candidates.title: Can anthropomorphic framing move judgments without performance?

sources.locator: Language-understanding and sociotechnical-risk discussions
sources.use: Separate interpretation of fluent outputs from measured behavior.
sources.boundary: A framing effect would not refute understanding or decide normative claims.

sources.locator: Original subjective, behavioral and physiological endpoint distinction; replication challenge
sources.use: Transfer endpoint-specific intervention logic.
sources.boundary: No bodily-posture mechanism or empirical effect size transfers.

candidates.mechanism: Descriptions can influence evaluations without changing the underlying artifact. Transfer endpoint separation to an automated judge audit: manipulate anthropomorphic versus mechanical labels around identical outputs, while executable correctness remains fixed and separately recorded.
candidates.hypothesis: An automated judge susceptible to framing will change attributed-understanding scores by at least 0.5 on a seven-point scale across labels, while identical outputs retain identical correctness; a gap below 0.2 favors framing robustness.
candidates.experiment: Freeze 100 synthetic programming/logic outputs, balanced correct/incorrect by hidden tests. Present each output under randomized anthropomorphic, mechanical and neutral labels to a fixed local judge in isolated contexts; preregister rubric, order and thresholds.
candidates.baseline: Identical output bytes and equal judge-token budgets; correctness comes from the same executable tests, not judge agreement. Use artifact as the paired unit.
candidates.metric: Within-output label effect on understanding and correctness judgments, against invariant test results; report artifact-bootstrap intervals.
candidates.falsifier: A narrow effect interval within ±0.2 weakens the framing hypothesis. A >0.5 shift confined to interpretive ratings supports judgment sensitivity without proving anything about genuine understanding.
candidates.confound: Label text can leak intended ratings; use equal-length symmetric templates and include neutral-label repetition for stochastic variation.
candidates.feasibility: 300 automated judgments plus executable tests; evaluates a judge, not human susceptibility or ethical acceptability.

candidates.title: A replication passport for changing model builds

sources.locator: Early-model disclosure; §10 limitations
sources.use: Record which model, prompts and endpoints are actually reproducible.
sources.boundary: Unavailable early GPT-4 cannot be exactly replicated with a newer build.

sources.locator: Original nine experiments; Failing the Future retroactive-recall replications; 90-experiment follow-up
sources.use: Transfer endpoint-matched, leakage-controlled replication boundaries.
sources.boundary: Recall replication results do not adjudicate every Bem paradigm or any AI claim.

candidates.mechanism: A replication label can conceal a changed endpoint or system. Transfer paradigm matching from the Bem dispute into a machine-readable passport separating same-build reruns, template transfer and cross-build conceptual follow-ups before any AI result is compared.
candidates.hypothesis: For one frozen model, task-template transfer will reduce accuracy by at least 0.15 relative to same-template reruns if apparent reliability depends on presentation; a gap below 0.05 favors template robustness.
candidates.experiment: Preregister 80 synthetic task families, three equivalent templates and two fixed-seed runs. Archive model/tokenizer hashes, prompt bytes and all outcomes. Analyze same-build reproducibility and template transfer separately; any second model becomes a conceptual extension.
candidates.baseline: Same task families, decoding parameters and per-query token cap. Matched rerun and transfer contrasts use family averages, not individual prompts as independent observations.
candidates.metric: Exact-output repeatability, answer consistency and the template-transfer accuracy gap with family-bootstrap intervals.
candidates.falsifier: A narrow transfer gap under 0.05 weakens template dependence; a gap above 0.15 despite repeatable same-template outputs favors presentation-limited reliability.
candidates.confound: Equivalent templates might inadvertently differ in information; validate every template against a symbolic solver and archive rejected templates.
candidates.feasibility: 480 small local generations; no claimed reproduction of historical GPT-4 or of Bem's human experiments.

candidates.title: Replicate claim-specific audits, not whole-paper verdicts

sources.locator: Training-data curation, environmental costs and language-understanding sections
sources.use: Build separate empirical, conceptual and normative claim ledgers.
sources.boundary: A capability result cannot falsify the paper as a whole or settle its values.

sources.locator: Hormone/risk/self-report endpoints; larger replication; broader synthesis
sources.use: Transfer endpoint-matched replication bookkeeping.
sources.boundary: Later subjective-posture evidence is not a direct replication of every original endpoint.

candidates.mechanism: A whole-paper verdict conflates claims requiring different evidence. Transfer endpoint-specific replication bookkeeping to an AI argument audit, checking whether independently rerun extraction preserves the boundary between a measurable proposition, an interpretation and an ethical judgment.
candidates.hypothesis: A typed claim ledger will reduce invalid whole-paper refutation links by at least 30 percentage points versus an untyped summary when both process identical constructed evidence packets.
candidates.experiment: Construct 90 synthetic claim/evidence packets with author-written answer keys, balanced empirical/conceptual/normative and mixed-strength evidence. Freeze two extraction prompts; run isolated contexts twice. Include deliberately irrelevant capability successes and endpoint-mismatched follow-ups.
candidates.baseline: Equal packet counts, model, context and output-token budget; typed versus untyped extraction. Packet is the independent unit; exact keys encode scope relations rather than contested philosophical truth.
candidates.metric: Invalid-refutation rate, correct scope-link rate, omission rate and rerun agreement; paired packet-bootstrap intervals.
candidates.falsifier: A narrow improvement below 10 points or a compensating omission increase favors no useful ledger benefit; ≥30 points without omission inflation supports improved scope bookkeeping.
candidates.confound: Synthetic keys may privilege the ledger vocabulary; counterbalance wording and reserve paraphrased packet families before prompt design.
candidates.feasibility: 360 short local generations. This tests bookkeeping on constructed examples, not the truth of Parrots or power posing.

candidates.title: Task-family weighting versus the showcase average

sources.locator: §1.1 exploratory demonstration scope; §8 and §10 limitations
sources.use: Make the sampling unit behind a broad capability summary explicit.
sources.boundary: Synthetic sampling cannot reconstruct undocumented historical selection decisions.

sources.locator: Country/year inclusion and weighting in original, critical replication and author response
sources.use: Transfer inclusion and aggregation sensitivity analysis.
sources.boundary: Corrected association does not establish a debt threshold, nor does weighting establish AI generality.

candidates.mechanism: Overrepresented easy families can dominate a pooled success rate. Transfer inclusion and weighting audits from historical economic summaries to AI demonstrations, retaining all generated tasks and showing exactly which family weights produce the reported capability headline.
candidates.hypothesis: A deliberately imbalanced showcase sample will overstate equal-family held-out accuracy by at least 0.15; balanced reporting should reduce that inflation below 0.05 when evaluated against the same known task population.
candidates.experiment: Preregister 12 synthetic task families, 20 instances each, and a sealed 10-per-family holdout. Freeze local model and scoring. Compare random showcases with an explicitly simulated curator selecting easy-family examples; audit all inclusions.
candidates.baseline: Equal showcase size and total generated-response budget. Compare pooled, equal-family and holdout-standardized estimates using the same outputs; never infer unobserved Sparks selection.
candidates.metric: Headline-minus-heldout accuracy, family coverage and worst-family accuracy; repeat sampling 1,000 times from the fixed output pool.
candidates.falsifier: Inflation below 0.05 even under specified imbalance favors robust aggregation; ≥0.15 inflation removed by balancing supports the proposed selection diagnostic.
candidates.confound: Task families may differ in semantic overlap, not only difficulty; publish generator definitions and stratify overlap using known construction labels.
candidates.feasibility: 360 local generations, then cheap resampling. Establishes an audit failure mode, not that the focal paper exhibits it.

candidates.title: A discovery-and-confirmation firewall for capability search

sources.locator: Exploratory task examples and §10 limitations
sources.use: Keep exploratory demonstrations distinct from locked confirmatory tests.
sources.boundary: Exploration is useful; this protocol makes no allegation about the authors' search history.

sources.locator: Original experimental set, retroactive-recall replications and 90-experiment meta-analysis
sources.use: Transfer prospective endpoint choice and selection sensitivity.
sources.boundary: No pooled effect or failed paradigm transfers to model competence.

candidates.mechanism: Trying many prompts can discover a useful interface and also select lucky outcomes. Transfer prospective replication discipline into a capability-search firewall: spend a fixed discovery budget, then lock the prompt and evaluate untouched task families with all attempts retained.
candidates.hypothesis: Selecting the best of 20 prompts on a small discovery set will produce a discovery-to-confirmation gap at least 0.10 larger than a preregistered fixed prompt under a matched total token budget.
candidates.experiment: Use 100 synthetic task families split before generation into discovery and sealed confirmation. Prespecify 20 wording variants. Allocate a fixed token budget to prompt search and confirmation; run 30 resampled family splits on a reusable fixed response matrix.
candidates.baseline: A fixed-prompt condition receives the identical overall response-token budget, with surplus spent on additional confirmation families; compare at equal total cost and report both equal-family subsets and expanded confirmation.
candidates.metric: Optimism gap, held-out correct families per million tokens, prompt-rank stability and family-level uncertainty.
candidates.falsifier: No excess optimism plus greater held-out correct families per token favors productive prompt discovery; a large gap with no budget-adjusted gain favors selection overfitting.
candidates.confound: Prompt search can be a legitimate part of the deployed system; define the evaluated system to include search and report its cost, not only the winning prompt.
candidates.feasibility: Up to 2,000 short offline generations with a hard token ceiling; simulation/resampling evaluates the protocol, not historical experiments.

candidates.title: Endpoint-preserving score translation

sources.locator: Original PubMed 20855902; robustness replication PubMed 25810452; broader meta-analysis DOI 10.1037/bul0000356
sources.use: Keep hormone, risk-taking and subjective-feeling outcomes in separate measurement channels when interpreting replication.
sources.boundary: A broader posture literature cannot be relabeled a direct replication of the original hormonal result.

sources.locator: Sparks v5, arXiv 2303.12712, sections 1.1 and 10; related metric critique arXiv 2304.15004
sources.use: Transfer the lesson that conclusions can depend on score construction and task thresholds.
sources.boundary: The related emergence-metric critique is not a direct replication of Sparks and supplies no psychology effect sizes.

candidates.mechanism: Represent each claim with an endpoint identity and score definition before aggregation. A synthetic audit varies scoring thresholds while holding observations fixed, testing whether apparent cross-endpoint agreement is created by recoding rather than shared evidence.
candidates.hypothesis: A typed scoring pipeline will reject unsupported hormone-to-subjective generalization while preserving evidence that genuinely concerns the same endpoint.
candidates.experiment: Offline pilot: generate 120 synthetic study summaries, 40 per endpoint class, with fixed known effects and measurement scales; include null-hormone/positive-subjective and concordant-effect scenarios. Compare an endpoint-typed parser and an untyped pooling parser on the identical summaries and 24 predeclared recoding perturbations. The sample unit is a synthetic study summary; each method receives the same summaries and number of scoring passes. Use only public abstract/metadata statements to define endpoint labels, not to invent original participant values.
candidates.baseline: Untyped standardized-score aggregation plus a simple endpoint-stratified table; match the number of summaries, perturbations and output assertions.
candidates.metric: Unsupported cross-endpoint assertions per 100 outputs; same-endpoint recovery rate; conclusion changes under score-only transformations.
candidates.falsifier: If the simple endpoint-stratified table matches the typed pipeline on error rate and recovery across all seeded scenarios, favor endpoint stratification alone over the proposed richer representation. If scoring changes alter conclusions even within endpoint-matched continuous analyses, investigate scale sensitivity rather than endpoint confusion.
candidates.confound: Artificially obvious labels may make the audit trivial. Include predeclared ambiguous outcome descriptions and require an unknown label instead of a forced classification.
candidates.feasibility: Small deterministic offline generator and assertion checker; no participant recruitment, causal claims about posture or new model-capability experiments.

candidates.title: Evidence-unit ledger before meta-analysis

sources.locator: Original nine experiments, PMID 21280961; Failing the Future, PMC3303812; 90-experiment meta-analysis, F1000Research 4-1188
sources.use: Distinguish particular retroactive-recall replications from a pooled collection of paradigms and outcomes.
sources.boundary: A favorable author-led pooled estimate and failed recall replications have different evidence units; neither can be substituted for the other.

sources.locator: Original NBER w4509; 2000 comment DOI 10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; reply DOI 10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Transfer attention to payroll-versus-survey measurement, sample construction and paired observational units.
sources.boundary: Restaurant employment measurement disagreements are methodological analogies, not evidence for or against anomalous cognition.

candidates.mechanism: Assign study, sample, paradigm and outcome identifiers before combining reports. A provenance ledger separates repeated analyses of one sample from independent replications, analogous to separating alternate employment measurements from additional restaurants.
candidates.hypothesis: Deduplicating at the sample-and-paradigm level will prevent confidence gains caused solely by counting alternate reports as independent evidence.
candidates.experiment: Construct 60 synthetic base experiments in three paradigm groups, then produce 180 report records with disclosed sample overlap, alternate outcomes and mixed paradigm labels. Create two conditions with identical report counts: true independent samples and duplicated samples. Compare ledger-aware and report-level summaries with the same fixed effect estimator. The unit for uncertainty is the base experiment; allocate the same 180-record parsing budget and estimator calls to both pipelines. Public BEM follow-ups determine the ledger fields, not simulated effect magnitudes.
candidates.baseline: Report-level pooling and a paper-ID deduplication baseline; both receive the same records.
candidates.metric: Coverage of synthetic 95% intervals across 500 seeded datasets; effective independent-unit count error; correct separation of recall-specific and broader-paradigm claims.
candidates.falsifier: If paper-ID deduplication gives calibrated coverage and correct paradigm scope under the same overlap patterns, favor the simpler ledger. If interval failure persists after exact sample deduplication, correlated outcomes or estimator assumptions are the stronger explanation.
candidates.confound: Unknown overlap in real publications cannot be solved by assigning IDs. The offline audit must include unresolved overlap marked unknown and report uncertainty bounds.
candidates.feasibility: Synthetic records and public evidence metadata only; no original-data reanalysis and no new human study.

candidates.title: Time-arrow controls for retroactive-claim pipelines

sources.locator: Feeling the Future, PMID 21280961, retroactive-recall experiments; Failing the Future, PMC3303812
sources.use: Specify which outcome precedes which randomized future event and which recall paradigm is actually being tested.
sources.boundary: The failed direct replications concern retroactive facilitation of recall; they do not empirically cover every original experiment.

sources.locator: NBER w4509, before/after New Jersey–Pennsylvania comparison; comment/reply DOI 10.1257/aer.90.5.1362 and 10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Transfer placebo timing and comparison-unit reasoning to distinguish pipeline artifacts from a temporally specific estimand.
sources.boundary: A natural experiment and a randomized cognition paradigm have different identifying assumptions; no economic effect or causal conclusion transfers.

candidates.mechanism: Treat temporal ordering as an executable data contract. Synthetic event streams include hidden look-ahead, time-index drift and selection on future information; predeclared placebo contrasts expose associations that a nominally retroactive test can inherit from bookkeeping.
candidates.hypothesis: A time-index validator plus placebo-event contrasts will detect planted look-ahead artifacts with fewer false retroactive flags than an effect-only analysis.
candidates.experiment: Simulate 200 independent sessions per seed with observed recall fixed before a later randomized practice event. Across 100 seeds each, test null streams, an injected retroactive signal, index drift, and leakage during record selection. Compare equal-budget pipelines with 20 contrasts per seed: validation/placebos versus 20 ordinary resamples. The session is the independent unit. The injected signal is a software positive control, not a physical model or empirical evidence that retrocausation occurs.
candidates.baseline: The same recall contrast without timing validation; ordinary resampling uses the identical contrast count and generated sessions.
candidates.metric: Artifact-detection sensitivity at a fixed 5% null flag rate; correct classification of planted artifacts versus clean injected signals; contract violations localized per session.
candidates.falsifier: If clean-null and clean-injected-signal streams are flagged equally often as leaked streams, the temporal controls lack discrimination. If ordinary resampling detects all planted artifacts at matched false-positive rate, favor that simpler pipeline.
candidates.confound: Controls tailored only to the planted leakage family can overstate usefulness. Reserve a blinded synthetic artifact family and publish sensitivity by family.
candidates.feasibility: An offline event-log test suite; any preregistered human replication remains future work requiring its own approvals and design.

candidates.title: Separate posture totals from post-treatment pathways

sources.locator: Original PMID 20855902, hormone/risk/self-report outcomes; larger replication PMID 25810452; meta-analysis DOI 10.1037/bul0000356
sources.use: Keep original outcomes separate and clarify whether analysis targets assignment, subjective experience or physiological pathways.
sources.boundary: The offline exercise cannot establish whether any real posture effect exists; subjective and endocrine endpoints remain distinct.

sources.locator: Growth in a Time of Debt, DOI 10.1257/aer.100.2.573; Herndon–Ash–Pollin critical replication; Reinhart–Rogoff April 2013 response
sources.use: Transfer the distinction between a reproducible association and a causal claim, with explicit estimands before adjustment.
sources.boundary: Country-level debt confounding does not imply randomized posture assignment has the same confounding problem.

candidates.mechanism: An estimand-first graph records which variables precede assignment and which could be mediators. Simulated posture trials demonstrate how controlling for post-treatment subjective feelings can change the estimated total effect without resolving the underlying endocrine dispute.
candidates.hypothesis: An adjustment checker tied to an explicit total-effect estimand will avoid mediator and collider bias more reliably than a rule that adjusts for every measured correlate.
candidates.experiment: Generate 1,000 synthetic randomized two-arm datasets of 240 independent participant records, using four predeclared DAGs: pure null, subjective-only pathway, mediated endocrine pathway and post-treatment collider. Fit three fixed models per dataset with identical records and compute budgets: unadjusted assignment contrast, all-covariate adjustment, and estimand-approved adjustment. Sample sizes and pathways are illustrative, not reconstructed original power-posing data. Evaluate hormone and subjective outcomes separately.
candidates.baseline: Unadjusted randomized contrast and indiscriminate all-covariate regression; all receive the same covariate table and three-model budget.
candidates.metric: Bias and interval coverage for the known synthetic total effect, by endpoint and DAG; frequency of correct refusal to interpret an adjusted association as a total effect.
candidates.falsifier: If unadjusted contrasts match the checker across every randomized scenario, favor the simpler unadjusted analysis for total effects. If the checker fails under an omitted mediator-outcome confounder, favor an explicitly unidentified pathway conclusion over a mediation claim.
candidates.confound: Correct graph specification supplies information unavailable from data alone. Report performance with wrong graphs and unknown temporal roles, not just oracle graphs.
candidates.feasibility: Offline simulation and model-audit specification; no hormone sampling, intervention or original-data reanalysis.

candidates.title: Replication passports with version-sensitive scope

sources.locator: Original PMID 21280961, nine experiments; PMC3303812, three recall replication attempts; F1000Research 4-1188, 90-experiment synthesis
sources.use: Make paradigm, timing and outcome fidelity explicit before assigning a direct-replication label.
sources.boundary: Broad favorable synthesis cannot erase a recall-specific failure, and a recall-specific failure cannot be relabeled a test of all nine experiments.

sources.locator: Sparks v5 arXiv 2303.12712, sections 1.1 and 10 and early-model disclosure
sources.use: Transfer version and procedure identity requirements from evaluation of an early proprietary model.
sources.boundary: A later model is not the original model; version mismatch is a scope limit, not an automatic excuse for a failed test.

candidates.mechanism: A replication passport separates exact procedure identity, justified functional equivalence and unknown deviations. Cross-domain version tracking supplies a disciplined way to label what a replication can test without letting every unfavorable result be dismissed as different.
candidates.hypothesis: A locked passport taxonomy will reduce both false direct-replication labels and post-hoc exemption of unfavorable results.
candidates.experiment: Prepare 80 synthetic protocol pairs varying one predeclared field at a time: recall paradigm, event order, outcome, randomization, software timing or unavailable implementation version. A rule-based classifier sees only protocol differences; a result-aware baseline additionally sees a randomly assigned favorable/unfavorable label. The unit is a protocol pair; both use the same 80 pairs and one classification pass. Ground field definitions in the primary BEM and Sparks disclosures; do not invent details of inaccessible protocols.
candidates.baseline: An endpoint-only matching rule and a permissive similarity rule, each fixed before outcome labels are revealed.
candidates.metric: Classification agreement with a published deterministic rubric; label invariance when favorable/unfavorable results are swapped; unknown-versus-direct misclassification rate.
candidates.falsifier: If endpoint-only matching achieves the same scope classification and outcome-label invariance, favor the simpler rule. If reasonable rubric choices materially reverse labels, report unresolved procedural equivalence rather than claim the passport resolves replication.
candidates.confound: A rubric authored by the same team is not ground truth. Predeclare alternate defensible rubrics and report disagreements; keep missing fields unknown.
candidates.feasibility: Offline protocol-metadata exercise; no new participants or later-model capability test is run.

candidates.title: Crossed measurement-and-context replication atlas

sources.locator: Original PMID 20855902; larger replication PMID 25810452; broader meta-analysis DOI 10.1037/bul0000356; daily-life follow-up PMID 40534239
sources.use: Separate endpoint changes from intervention/context changes when comparing laboratory and later posture studies.
sources.boundary: A later daily-life follow-up is not an exact replication of the original hormone or risk experiment.

sources.locator: Original NBER w4509; payroll challenge DOI 10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; administrative-data reply DOI 10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Transfer a crossed design that distinguishes changed measurement from changed samples or contexts.
sources.boundary: The specific wage-policy episode does not determine whether posture findings generalize.

candidates.mechanism: Cross context with measurement method rather than changing both together. Synthetic multi-site datasets reveal when apparent replication differences arise from instrument construction, true context moderation or both, while maintaining separate hormone, subjective and behavioral outcomes.
candidates.hypothesis: A balanced context-by-measurement atlas will distinguish measurement artifacts from context heterogeneity more accurately than a collection where each site uses its own instrument.
candidates.experiment: Generate 12 synthetic sites with 80 independent participant records each, three endpoint channels and two alternate measurement mappings per record. In separate known scenarios plant only measurement bias, only context moderation, both or neither. Compare crossed and confounded allocations at 960 participant records and the same 1,920 measurement evaluations per endpoint. Repeat 200 seeds. Synthetic paired measurements are explicitly constructed; no claim is made that real hormone and self-report measures share a latent scale.
candidates.baseline: Site-specific instruments without crossing; a same-instrument-only pooled analysis; match participant and measurement budgets.
candidates.metric: Correct identification of the planted source of heterogeneity; false moderation rate; held-out-site predictive error reported separately for each endpoint.
candidates.falsifier: If the crossed allocation cannot distinguish measurement-only from context-only scenarios above the predeclared chance baseline, favor non-identifiability. If a single harmonized instrument performs equally well under matched budgets, prefer harmonization over the more complex atlas.
candidates.confound: Two synthetic mappings of one record are dependent. Cluster uncertainty by participant and site; include instrument-by-context interaction that violates simple additive decomposition.
candidates.feasibility: Offline simulation plus a public protocol template; collecting any crossed human replication is separate future work.

candidates.title: Selection stress maps with locked evidence units

sources.locator: Feeling the Future PMID 21280961; recall replications PMC3303812; author-led 90-experiment meta-analysis F1000Research 4-1188
sources.use: Audit how paradigm inclusion, outcome choice and publication selection affect pooled summaries without conflating different tests.
sources.boundary: A synthetic selection mechanism cannot establish that any particular author used that mechanism or estimate the real extent of publication bias.

sources.locator: Original DOI 10.1257/aer.100.2.573; Herndon–Ash–Pollin replication, coding/inclusion/weighting analyses; Reinhart–Rogoff April 2013 response
sources.use: Transfer explicit inclusion and weighting sensitivity from a documented reproducibility correction.
sources.boundary: A documented spreadsheet error in economics is not evidence of an analogous error, misconduct or retraction in psychology.

candidates.mechanism: Factor the analysis into eligible evidence units, admissible exclusions and weights. A predeclared sensitivity grid measures which conclusions survive these choices, distinguishing a correctable implementation error from a conclusion that depends on selective aggregation.
candidates.hypothesis: A locked multiverse will correctly localize whether a synthetic pooled effect changes because of weighting, missing null studies or outcome selection.
candidates.experiment: Simulate 100 base experiments in four distinct paradigm strata, then expose report collections under four known selection mechanisms. Evaluate a fixed 3-by-3-by-3 grid of weighting, admissible-inclusion and outcome rules, always showing stratum-specific results before any pooled value. Use 200 seeded corpora per mechanism; the unit is the base experiment. Give every pipeline exactly 27 estimations per corpus and identical visible records. Withheld studies are known only to the scoring harness.
candidates.baseline: One preferred pooled specification and 27 random admissible specifications; identical estimator budget and visible evidence.
candidates.metric: Recovery of the planted sensitivity source; coverage of true synthetic stratum effects; number of sign conclusions stable across all declared choices.
candidates.falsifier: If random specifications localize the planted selection source as well as the structured grid, favor the simpler search. If all admissible choices remain biased under hidden missingness, favor an unidentified missing-evidence conclusion rather than interpreting stability as validity.
candidates.confound: The visible multiverse cannot recover studies never observed. Include missing-not-at-random scenarios and state that stability within visible evidence does not resolve them.
candidates.feasibility: Synthetic experiment-level audit; no actual meta-analysis effect is recomputed or attributed to a paper.

candidates.title: A discovery-to-confirmation firewall for persuasive examples

sources.locator: Original PMID 20855902, separate hormones/risk/self-report; larger replication PMID 25810452; broader synthesis DOI 10.1037/bul0000356
sources.use: Prevent favorable endpoint selection from being presented as confirmation of the original multi-endpoint claim.
sources.boundary: The audit tests a selection procedure, not whether real posture outcomes were intentionally cherry-picked.

sources.locator: Sparks v5 arXiv 2303.12712, sections 1.1, 8 and 10
sources.use: Transfer the distinction between exploratory selected demonstrations and a locked confirmatory evaluation.
sources.boundary: Selected demonstrations can be informative; their existence does not supply a calibrated population success rate or resolve a general-intelligence definition.

candidates.mechanism: Keep an immutable discovery ledger, then freeze endpoint identities and success criteria before a held-out confirmation stage. Synthetic searches quantify how selecting persuasive examples inflates apparent reliability even when each displayed result is reported accurately.
candidates.hypothesis: A discovery/confirmation firewall will reduce winner's-curse inflation while retaining more true signals than merely demanding a stricter threshold on selected discovery results.
candidates.experiment: Generate 300 synthetic research campaigns, each with 30 candidate contrasts distributed across hormone, risk and subjective endpoint families. Discovery and confirmation each receive 120 independent synthetic records per campaign. Allocate a fixed 60 contrast evaluations: 30 discovery plus 30 locked confirmation. Compare with 60 discovery-only evaluations using a predeclared adjusted threshold. Include null, sparse-signal and endpoint-specific-signal scenarios; no original participants or model outputs enter the simulation.
candidates.baseline: Discovery-only top-result selection, with and without multiplicity adjustment; hold total synthetic records and contrast evaluations equal by splitting versus pooling the same 240-record budget.
candidates.metric: Selected-effect inflation, false confirmation rate, true-signal recovery and endpoint-identity violations; report all by planted endpoint family.
candidates.falsifier: If the multiplicity-adjusted discovery-only method matches confirmation error and exceeds true-signal recovery at the same budget, favor that alternative. If the firewall fails when confirmation shares hidden batch effects, favor an independently generated confirmation dataset over administrative separation alone.
candidates.confound: Artificial independence between discovery and confirmation makes the firewall look too strong. Add a predeclared shared-batch scenario and analyze its failure separately.
candidates.feasibility: Offline simulation and append-only ledger prototype; no human experiment or new model benchmark is executed.

candidates.title: Separate employment endpoints before comparing minimum-wage results

sources.locator: Card–Krueger original https://www.nber.org/papers/w4509; Neumark–Wascher comment https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; Card–Krueger reply https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Keep survey, payroll and administrative employment constructions and sample frames separately identifiable.
sources.boundary: The reply remains attached to the challenge; no source is treated as establishing a universal wage effect.

sources.locator: Original endpoints https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20855902/; robustness study https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25810452/; endpoint-specific synthesis https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000356
sources.use: Transfer the requirement to distinguish physiological, behavioral and subjective endpoints into a ledger of distinct employment estimands.
sources.boundary: No posture effect size or evidence strength transfers to labor markets; distinguishing endpoints does not automatically reconcile estimates.

candidates.mechanism: An endpoint ledger prevents headcount, full-time-equivalent staffing, hours and establishment survival from silently substituting for one another. Synthetic records permit controlled changes to each quantity while holding the others fixed, revealing whether a disagreement arises from measurement or persists under a shared estimand.
candidates.hypothesis: When artificial datasets encode identical hours but different full-time/part-time composition, a shared endpoint ledger reduces false declarations of contradictory employment effects relative to a single-label employment comparison.
candidates.experiment: Offline, preregister 40 synthetic state-pair policy episodes with 80 establishments each. Independently vary staffing composition, hours, survival and survey error; retain known truth for every endpoint. Create survey, payroll and administrative-like extracts with explicit overlap. Compare a ledger workflow against a one-endpoint-label workflow with equal 24-analysis budgets and identical records. Score recovery by endpoint and aggregate uncertainty over policy episodes, not establishments as independent policy assignments.
candidates.baseline: One employment column per extract with a common units label; identical available observations, analytical budget and estimator.
candidates.metric: Wrong-sign claims against endpoint-specific synthetic truth; endpoint mismatch detection sensitivity and specificity; coverage of episode-cluster uncertainty intervals.
candidates.falsifier: If disagreements and error rates persist after exact endpoint and sample alignment, measurement mismatch is insufficient. If the ledger induces extra exclusions or no lower wrong-sign rate, prefer the simpler common-endpoint workflow.
candidates.confound: Synthetic error may omit strategic reporting or unobserved management responses. Neither payroll status nor administrative coverage guarantees accurate hours or an exogenous comparator.
candidates.feasibility: One Python simulation plus a machine-readable endpoint dictionary; no original-data reanalysis, employer contact or policy intervention is required.

candidates.title: Stress-test apparent debt thresholds against binning artifacts

sources.locator: Original debt bins https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.100.2.573; Herndon–Ash–Pollin replication https://peri.umass.edu/publication/does-high-public-debt-consistently-stifle-economic-growth-a-critique-of-reinhart-and-rogoff/; author response https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rogoff/files/debt_growth_and_the_austerity_debate.pdf
sources.use: Represent threshold, inclusion and weighting choices as separate measurement operations while retaining the response's broader-association defense.
sources.boundary: A corrected descriptive association can remain without a sharp threshold or identified causal effect.

sources.locator: Original exploratory demonstrations and limitations https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.12712v5; related methodological challenge https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.15004
sources.use: Transfer continuous-versus-discrete metric stress tests from the emergent-abilities discussion to binned debt-growth summaries.
sources.boundary: The metric-artifact paper is not a direct replication of Sparks; neither its results nor AI capability claims determine debt-growth behavior.

candidates.mechanism: A smooth relationship can acquire an apparent jump when observations are discretized and unevenly weighted. Compare binned summaries with smooth and genuine-change-point alternatives on synthetic panels where the response shape is known, separating estimator artifacts from detectable structural changes.
candidates.hypothesis: Under smooth synthetic debt-growth relationships and unequal country histories, prespecified neighboring-bin contrasts produce more false threshold declarations than held-out change-point tests calibrated to the same false-positive budget.
candidates.experiment: Generate 60 synthetic country panels with 25 years each under three worlds: no relation, smooth negative association and true change point. Vary unequal observation lengths and serial dependence independently. Freeze 12 binned/smooth/change-point procedures before revealing world labels; give each equal training observations and held-out-country folds. Repeat 100 seeds and bootstrap entire countries. Include the original-style debt bins as one documented descriptive procedure, not an assumed ground truth.
candidates.baseline: Prespecified binned high-versus-low summary with its declared weighting; compare at matched nominal false-positive rate and equal procedure-selection budget.
candidates.metric: False threshold rate in smooth worlds; threshold localization and power in change-point worlds; held-out-country prediction error; weighting sensitivity.
candidates.falsifier: If matched-budget binned contrasts control false positives and locate genuine breaks as well as alternatives, the proposed stress test adds little. A stable break favoring the change-point world would count against a pure binning-artifact explanation.
candidates.confound: Synthetic debt measurement may omit valuation revisions and crisis-specific reporting. Real reverse causality and omitted institutions remain unmeasured and cannot be settled by this measurement audit.
candidates.feasibility: Offline panel simulation and transparent summaries; no causal policy recommendation or claim about the real threshold follows.

candidates.title: Use time-direction placebos to expose debt-growth identification limits

sources.locator: Original historical association https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.100.2.573; critical reconstruction https://peri.umass.edu/publication/does-high-public-debt-consistently-stifle-economic-growth-a-critique-of-reinhart-and-rogoff/; response https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rogoff/files/debt_growth_and_the_austerity_debate.pdf
sources.use: Separate reproducing corrected aggregates from distinguishing debt-causes-growth, growth-causes-debt and common-shock explanations.
sources.boundary: The response's broader association remains compatible with multiple causal graphs; this audit does not infer authors' motives.

sources.locator: Original nine experiments https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21280961/; recall-specific direct replications https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3303812/; favorable pooled follow-up https://f1000research.com/articles/4-1188
sources.use: Transfer locked time order, endpoint-specific tests and temporal-leakage controls into synthetic panel identification challenges.
sources.boundary: Future outcomes can statistically predict current economic variables without retrocausality; a placebo failure diagnoses model assumptions, not paranormal influence or every original Bem endpoint.

candidates.mechanism: Known-direction synthetic panels provide a blind identification challenge: analysts must distinguish a causal exposure effect from reverse feedback and persistent common shocks. Time-shifted placebo exposures reveal some failures, while deliberately observationally similar worlds reveal cases where the correct output is underidentification.
candidates.hypothesis: Adding prespecified time-direction placebos and an explicit underidentified verdict reduces confident wrong-direction claims relative to contemporaneous association alone, without claiming that passing placebos proves causation.
candidates.experiment: Generate 90 synthetic 50-country, 30-year panels divided equally among debt-to-growth, growth-to-debt and latent-crisis-common-cause worlds. Include serial dependence and overlapping observable summaries; reserve world labels. Compare an association-only classifier and a graph-plus-placebo workflow with the same 10 fits per panel. Hold out whole countries and whole synthetic worlds; calibrate uncertainty by country. Permit both workflows to abstain under an identical stated loss function.
candidates.baseline: Contemporaneous and lagged associations with equal fit budget and the same abstention option; no randomized-policy interpretation.
candidates.metric: Wrong confident causal-direction rate; abstention versus identification accuracy; detection of deliberate temporal leakage; calibration by causal world.
candidates.falsifier: If time placebos pass equally in confounded and causal worlds and the workflow still overclaims, they do not discriminate the hypotheses. If baseline abstention achieves equal calibration and accuracy, prefer that simpler procedure.
candidates.confound: Latent crisis severity, institutional changes and measurement revisions may defeat all chosen controls. Multiple real causal pathways can coexist; the simulation's exclusive worlds simplify that possibility.
candidates.feasibility: A bounded offline simulator and blinded labels; no new causal claim about actual country histories or debt policy.

candidates.title: Separate wage estimands, identification assumptions and policy values

sources.locator: Original state comparison https://www.nber.org/papers/w4509; payroll comment https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; administrative-data reply https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Keep the episode-specific comparison and measurement dispute attached while auditing comparison trends, spillovers and employment definitions.
sources.boundary: An episode-specific employment estimate does not determine all wage effects or whether a policy is desirable.

sources.locator: Original sociotechnical argument https://doi.org/10.1145/3442188.3445922; contrasting demonstrations https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.12712v5; conceptual distinctions https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.03551
sources.use: Transfer claim decomposition: empirical performance, interpretation and normative consequences require separate evidence and decision rules.
sources.boundary: No finding about language meaning or environmental harms transfers to minimum-wage effects; this proposal tests an audit workflow, not ethical truth.

candidates.mechanism: A claim ledger distinguishes the numerical employment contrast, assumptions giving it a causal interpretation, and additional values needed for policy judgment. Synthetic counterfactual panels test whether this separation improves appropriate causal abstention when spillovers or differential trends undermine the neighboring-state comparison.
candidates.hypothesis: A graph-and-claim ledger reduces unsupported causal extrapolation across synthetic policy episodes relative to an estimate-only report, while retaining causal claims when the explicitly simulated identification assumptions hold.
candidates.experiment: Create 60 synthetic two-state policy episodes, each with 24 pre/post periods and 100 establishments per state. Factorially vary differential pretrends, cross-border spillovers and a latent demand shock; disclose only observed variables. Freeze both reporting workflows and give them six fits per episode. Blind held-out episode labels and score causal estimates and causal/associational/underidentified labels separately. Cluster assessment at policy episode; treat establishments as repeated observations.
candidates.baseline: Difference-in-differences estimate and interval with a conventional assumption paragraph; same data, six fits and permitted abstention.
candidates.metric: Coverage of episode-specific true effects; unsupported causal-label frequency; appropriate abstention under violated assumptions; specificity when assumptions hold. Policy preferences are unscored.
candidates.falsifier: If the ledger merely suppresses every causal conclusion or fails to flag confounded episodes, it has not improved identification. If estimates remain calibrated under simulated spillovers, the simpler workflow is favored for that world.
candidates.confound: Unobserved employer anticipation and consumer substitution can mimic favorable pretrends. Good pretrend diagnostics cannot prove parallel counterfactual trends or transport a local effect to other labor markets.
candidates.feasibility: Offline synthetic panels and rule-based report audits; no intervention, actual employer data or policy recommendation.

candidates.title: Keep debt spreadsheet reconstruction separate from causal replication

sources.locator: Original https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.100.2.573; replication code and data entry https://peri.umass.edu/publication/does-high-public-debt-consistently-stifle-economic-growth-a-critique-of-reinhart-and-rogoff/; author response https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rogoff/files/debt_growth_and_the_austerity_debate.pdf
sources.use: Define separate reproduction targets for spreadsheet range, country inclusion, weighting and the broader descriptive association defended in the response.
sources.boundary: Matching corrected aggregates validates reconstruction only; neither a match nor a mismatch identifies a causal debt threshold.

sources.locator: Original paradigms https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21280961/; three recall replications https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3303812/; author-led 90-experiment synthesis https://f1000research.com/articles/4-1188
sources.use: Transfer exact replication-target labeling and preserve scope differences between a specific paradigm and a pooled broader claim.
sources.boundary: Recall-replication outcomes and pooled psychological effects do not transfer to economic associations; the analogy concerns target matching.

candidates.mechanism: A layered replication manifest records what each result reproduces: data extraction, a specific aggregation, corrected descriptive association or a causal estimand. Mutation-tested synthetic spreadsheets reveal whether broad replication labels conceal a successful calculation coupled to an unsupported interpretation.
candidates.hypothesis: Layer-specific manifests detect more injected reconstruction errors and fewer false causal-validation claims than a single pass/fail replication badge under equal audit time.
candidates.experiment: Build 24 synthetic country-year spreadsheets with 30 countries and unequal 10–40-year histories. Inject one known defect per clone: off-by-one range, omitted country, changed year inclusion or equal-country versus equal-observation weighting. Publish exact checksums and expected descriptive outputs before a blinded audit. Compare layered and pass/fail reports with 20 checks each and matched input data. Score by independent workbook and aggregate country-level contribution diagnostics within each workbook.
candidates.baseline: A single aggregate checksum and pass/fail reproduction conclusion, with the same 20 allowed checks and access to the same manifest fields.
candidates.metric: Injected-defect localization accuracy; false failure on deliberate valid weighting variants; unsupported causal-validation statements; recovery of exact descriptive reference values.
candidates.falsifier: If layered labels do not improve localization or increase confusion between valid alternative estimands and coding defects, retain the simpler badge plus explicit scope statement. Matching values in a confounded world must never count as causal success.
candidates.confound: Cleanly injected spreadsheet defects may be easier than undocumented historical data revisions. Hidden changes in country definitions remain outside the fixture and could defeat exact reproduction.
candidates.feasibility: Small generated spreadsheets or CSVs and a deterministic audit harness; this is not a claimed reanalysis of the original economic dataset.

candidates.title: Version-lock the wage episode before testing transport to new settings

sources.locator: 1993 working paper / 1994 case study https://www.nber.org/papers/w4509; 2000 comment https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; 2000 reply https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Tag dataset vintage, sample construction and estimator so exact reconstruction is distinguished from new-data corroboration and new-episode transport.
sources.boundary: Both the comment and reply remain visible; administrative evidence is a distinct check, not automatic universal validation.

sources.locator: Early-model disclosure, exploratory examples and limitations https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.12712v5; metric-related challenge https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.15004
sources.use: Transfer model-build and task version locking into dataset-vintage and episode locking, with explicit separation of exact reruns from changed-system tests.
sources.boundary: A later model is not an exact replication of the early proprietary model; similarly a later wage episode is a transport test, not a rerun. No effect-size analogy is asserted.

candidates.mechanism: A versioned replication contract fixes input hashes, definitions and estimators before an exact rerun, then separately permits new measurement sources and new episodes. Synthetic counterexamples test whether provenance prevents expected contextual heterogeneity from being mislabeled as computational irreproducibility.
candidates.hypothesis: A three-tier exact-rerun, measurement-check and episode-transport contract reduces category errors relative to a flat replicated/not-replicated label without masking genuine implementation failures.
candidates.experiment: Generate 12 synthetic policy-episode families, each with one frozen original panel, a same-population alternate measurement, a changed-policy-context panel and an intentionally defective code rerun. Include both homogeneous and heterogeneous treatment-effect worlds. Assign equal 16-check budgets to flat-label and tiered workflows; hide defect/context labels until scoring. Evaluate by held-out episode family and use episode-family uncertainty, not establishment counts.
candidates.baseline: Flat replication label with the same data files, hashes and estimator choices available; equal audit effort and no additional observations.
candidates.metric: Four-way classification of exact reproduction, measurement disagreement, transport heterogeneity and software defect; missed-defect rate; unjustified universal-effect claims.
candidates.falsifier: If flat labels recover the distinctions equally well, tiering adds bureaucracy without value. If the tiered workflow excuses injected code failures as contextual variation, it fails the proposed mechanism.
candidates.confound: Dataset vintage can encode both measurement and genuine population change. Unmeasured institutional differences may make real transport discrepancies nondecomposable even with perfect hashes.
candidates.feasibility: Offline versioned synthetic datasets and deterministic labels; no original-data rerun, new survey, real policy inference or claim of exact GPT-4 replication.

candidates.title: Audit country-history selection before interpreting debt bins

sources.locator: Original inclusion and aggregation https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.100.2.573; critical replication https://peri.umass.edu/publication/does-high-public-debt-consistently-stifle-economic-growth-a-critique-of-reinhart-and-rogoff/; broader-association response https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rogoff/files/debt_growth_and_the_austerity_debate.pdf
sources.use: Keep country exclusions, year exclusions and country-versus-year weighting as separate declared selection mechanisms.
sources.boundary: Selection sensitivity can explain instability without proving every debt-growth association false; the original response remains an explicit alternative.

sources.locator: Original experiments https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21280961/; recall replication https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3303812/; favorable 90-experiment synthesis https://f1000research.com/articles/4-1188
sources.use: Transfer declared study-flow accounting and examination of selective inclusion into country-year contribution accounting.
sources.boundary: Countries are dependent historical units, not independent psychology experiments; no meta-analytic psychological result is imported.

candidates.mechanism: A contribution ledger exposes how country entry, observation duration and weighting alter an aggregate association. By generating known missingness mechanisms, the audit tests when transparent sample accounting can detect selection-driven sign changes and when unobserved selection leaves the result unresolved.
candidates.hypothesis: Country-history flow diagrams plus contribution bounds identify selection-induced reversals more reliably than a final-sample summary when missingness depends on observed country histories, but offer weaker discrimination under latent-crisis missingness.
candidates.experiment: Generate 100 synthetic 40-country panels with 40 years each. Impose random missingness, observed-history-dependent truncation and unobserved-crisis-dependent suppression at matched missing fractions. Compare final-sample analysis with a prespecified flow/contribution audit using equal 12 recomputations. Include both zero and negative full-panel associations. Draw held-out entire country histories and estimate uncertainty by country blocks; report each missingness world separately.
candidates.baseline: One declared complete-case country-year sample and its prespecified weighting, with the same 12 recomputations and metadata access.
candidates.metric: Detection of full-panel-to-observed sign reversals; specificity when no reversal exists; full-panel-summary interval coverage; sensitivity across missingness worlds.
candidates.falsifier: If the audit flags all incomplete panels indiscriminately or misses observed-selection reversals, its ledger has not discriminated the alternatives. Stable negative associations under all declared inclusions favor a robust descriptive association, still without identifying causality.
candidates.confound: Missing historical observations may depend on unrecorded wars, definitions and institutions. Bounds requiring observed-selection assumptions can be misleading under latent selection; those cases must remain unresolved.
candidates.feasibility: Offline generated panels and sample-flow reports; no access to original country histories or policy judgment is needed.

candidates.title: Distinguish wage sample attrition from endpoint selection

sources.locator: Original establishment survey https://www.nber.org/papers/w4509; payroll-based comment https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; reply with administrative analysis https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Compare respondent, payroll-available and administrative-covered establishment frames with common and frame-specific estimands.
sources.boundary: The comment and reply are rival measurement/coverage checks, not an assumed winner; the episode remains context-specific.

sources.locator: Original multiple outcomes https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20855902/; larger replication https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25810452/; broader preregistered synthesis https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000356
sources.use: Transfer outcome-family declaration and reporting of all endpoints to distinguish outcome cherry-picking from sample attrition.
sources.boundary: Physiological and subjective posture outcomes are not wage outcomes; this transfers selection-accounting methods, not conclusions about either paper.

candidates.mechanism: Crossing a fixed endpoint family with a fixed establishment-frame family separates two routes to apparent contradiction: choosing different employers and choosing different outcomes. A prespecified complete matrix makes selective presentation detectable while retaining genuine disagreement within matched cells.
candidates.hypothesis: A frame-by-endpoint audit reduces erroneous reconciliation of opposing estimates relative to a pooled narrative when synthetic disagreement is deliberately caused by sample selection, endpoint selection or true effect heterogeneity.
candidates.experiment: Generate 72 synthetic policy episodes, each with 200 establishments and known employment hours, headcount and survival. Independently vary response attrition, payroll availability and size-dependent treatment effects; include an unobserved manager-shock attrition world. Give both workflows the same 3 frames × 3 endpoints and exactly 9 estimator runs. Compare a preregistered full matrix with a pooled-summary workflow. Hold out complete policy episodes; calculate performance across episodes, not within-store observations as policy replicates.
candidates.baseline: A pooled report from the identical nine analyses and records with a declared primary endpoint, allowed to report disagreement but without mandatory frame-by-endpoint attribution.
candidates.metric: Correct attribution of disagreement to frame selection, endpoint selection, effect heterogeneity or unresolved mixture; false reconciliation rate; interval coverage for each declared frame-specific estimand.
candidates.falsifier: If disagreements persist within exactly matched frames and endpoints, sample/endpoint selection is insufficient and heterogeneity or bias remains plausible. If the full matrix does not improve blinded attribution or loses coverage through multiplicity, prefer the simpler report.
candidates.confound: Unobserved manager shocks can drive both attrition and employment, defeating observed-variable weighting. A closed establishment's absence must be distinguished from missing data; synthetic convenience cannot establish real nonresponse assumptions.
candidates.feasibility: A small offline factorial simulator and complete reporting table; no employer contact, new economic estimate, policy intervention or policy recommendation.

candidates.title: Four resource denominators, with unstable rankings left unresolved

sources.locator: Environmental-cost, opportunity-cost and language-understanding discussions
sources.use: Keep empirical resource accounting separate from conceptual and ethical claims.
sources.boundary: A local energy proxy cannot settle historical training emissions or social value.

sources.locator: Debt-bin aggregation; critical replication on weighting and inclusion; author response
sources.use: Audit how denominators and group weighting alter a summary.
sources.boundary: No debt threshold, causal direction or economics effect transfers.

candidates.mechanism: Different denominators answer different questions. Transfer the debt dispute's aggregation audit to AI resource evaluation: cost per request, cost per verified answer and cost per task family can rank the same systems differently without resolving ethical judgments.
candidates.hypothesis: If task-mix weighting matters, request-weighted and equal-family costs will reverse model ranking with paired intervals excluding a tie; stable orders favor robust rankings and overlapping intervals remain inconclusive.
candidates.experiment: Freeze two local models/tokenizers, hardware/runtime, decoding, formal-answer format, character caps and hidden tests. Use 80 synthetic families with prespecified 2/4/8 requests each, balanced difficulty/length strata, and three paired timing repetitions. Counterbalance execution order. Amortize fixed warm-up/loading costs over a declared deployment batch; prompt-search budget is zero. Report cached/uncached policies separately.

Seconds are primary; tokenizer-specific tokens are diagnostics, never emissions. Derive analytical reweighting predictions from stratum totals before interpreting observed reversals.

Near ties, nonfinite ratios or low accuracy leave ranking unresolved; report the accuracy/time frontier.

candidates.feasibility: Ceiling 2,500 short local generations including repetitions; no emissions, training-cost or ethical verdict. No run performed.
candidates.changes: Enumerated formulas and decision questions; added matched output requirements, achieved accuracy, overhead/search policy, repeated timing, analytical reweighting, zero-success handling and inconclusive rankings.

candidates.title: A randomized rule intervention with one paired estimand

sources.locator: §7.2.1, §8 and §10 capability examples and limitations
sources.use: Turn selected task performance into a narrowly defined intervention test.
sources.boundary: No single benchmark identifies general intelligence or exactly repeats early GPT-4.

sources.locator: Original NJ/PA before-after comparison; 2000 comment and reply
sources.use: Transfer explicit comparison-group and measurement assumptions.
sources.boundary: A synthetic randomized intervention does not inherit wage-study effects or policy validity.

candidates.mechanism: An answer may follow supplied evidence or remembered associations. Transfer comparison-group scrutiny into a randomized synthetic evidence intervention: preserve task form while changing only a fictional rule, and compare changes against an untouched matched rule.
candidates.hypothesis: Rule-specific updating predicts a positive affected-minus-unaffected contrast above a locked threshold; generic disruption predicts comparable changes in both question types or lost baseline correctness.
candidates.experiment: Create a disjoint 20-family pilot and 100-family confirmation set, each with two independent fictional rules and binary questions. Collect original, one-rule-flipped and length-matched sham conditions, asking both questions; randomize order and flipped rule. Freeze vocabulary/templates before confirmation. Keep generator seeds, solver keys and answer strings outside prompts; supply premises and questions only.
candidates.baseline: Same model, deterministic decoding, formal answer format and token cap for all six outputs per family. A symbolic solver validates changed and unchanged targets. Report original-rule accuracy separately from updating.
candidates.metric: Y_a,k=1 if affected answer equals the flipped target in condition k=flip or sham; Y_u,k=1 if companion answer equals its unchanged target. Estimate Δ=mean_f[(Y_a,flip−Y_a,sham)−(Y_u,flip−Y_u,sham)]. Probability means frequency across families, not repeated decoding. Report four component frequencies, original accuracy and paired family-bootstrap intervals.

Prospectively simulate precision for Δ=0,δ,0.60; retain 100 families if feasible, otherwise declare inadequate precision. Interval above δ with stable companions favors updating; near zero with equal degradation favors disruption. Low baseline accuracy, ceiling limits or intervals spanning explanations remain unresolved.
candidates.confound: Token/answer-position bias, malformed rules and sham salience; counterbalance labels, solver-check every item and retain failures without outcome-guided replacement.
candidates.feasibility: 720 short offline generations including pilot, plus simulations. No wage-effect transfer, historical GPT-4 replication or general-intelligence verdict. No run performed.
candidates.changes: Defined binary scoring and exact paired estimand; separated updating from accuracy, sealed keys/seeds, added pilot-locked thresholds and precision simulations, and specified unresolved low-accuracy/ceiling cases.

candidates.title: Template robustness with a replication passport

sources.locator: Early-model disclosure; §10 limitations
sources.use: Record which model, prompts and endpoints are actually reproducible.
sources.boundary: Unavailable early GPT-4 cannot be exactly replicated with a newer build.

sources.locator: Original nine experiments; Failing the Future retroactive-recall replications; 90-experiment follow-up
sources.use: Transfer endpoint-matched, leakage-controlled replication boundaries.
sources.boundary: Recall replication results do not adjudicate every Bem paradigm or any AI claim.

candidates.mechanism: Transfer paradigm matching from Bem into a replication passport. Test behavioral robustness across information-preserving templates for identical latent problems; treat computational determinism as a runtime diagnostic rather than evidence of general competence.
candidates.hypothesis: Presentation-sensitive competence predicts alternate-template accuracy at least 0.15 below reference; simultaneous paired intervals within ±0.05 for both alternates favor local template equivalence.
candidates.experiment: Use 80 latent synthetic problems, three templates and four prespecified stochastic seeds per template. Before calls validate identical logical content and target answers using canonical representations and a symbolic solver. Seal keys/seeds outside prompts. Archive model/tokenizer hashes, prompt bytes, runtime/container, accelerator/kernel and decoding settings.
candidates.baseline: Same latent problems, answer format and token cap across templates; shared seed labels permit pairing without assuming identical random trajectories. Separately rerun 20 reference prompts twice under fixed deterministic settings in one environment to diagnose computational repeatability.
candidates.metric: Average binary correctness over four seeds within each problem/template; estimate alternate-minus-reference differences separately for both alternates. Bootstrap latent problems with full seed/template blocks; use simultaneous intervals. Deterministic exact-output agreement is reported only as a runtime diagnostic.
