candidates.changes: Selected template robustness as outcome; separated deterministic checks from stochastic behavior, paired latent problems, specified information checks/sealed keys, runtime hashes, simultaneous margins and unresolved cases.

candidates.title: When balancing fixes showcase selection—and when it cannot

sources.locator: §1.1 exploratory demonstration scope; §8 and §10 limitations
sources.use: Make the sampling unit behind a broad capability summary explicit.
sources.boundary: Synthetic sampling cannot reconstruct undocumented historical selection decisions.

sources.locator: Country/year inclusion and weighting in original, critical replication and author response
sources.use: Transfer inclusion and aggregation sensitivity analysis.
sources.boundary: Corrected association does not establish a debt threshold, nor does weighting establish AI generality.

candidates.mechanism: Overrepresented easy families can dominate a pooled success rate. Transfer inclusion and weighting audits from historical economic summaries to AI demonstrations, retaining all generated tasks and showing exactly which family weights produce the reported capability headline.
candidates.hypothesis: Equal-family weighting should remove family-mix inflation under random within-family sampling, but may fail under within-family easy-item selection; unchanged gaps favor limited benefit from balancing.
candidates.experiment: Prespecify 12 synthetic families, with 20 pool and 10 sealed reference instances each, two decoding seeds per instance. Freeze model, format and caps. A disjoint pilot fixes family/item ease predictors without confirmation answers. Simulate 36-item showcases with softmax strengths β=0,1,3: family-biased, within-family-biased and balanced-but-within-family-biased selection. Reuse identical outputs for all summaries.
candidates.baseline: Matched 36-item showcases and shared generation budget; β=0 is random selection. No curator/reweighting step sees reference labels, and keys remain outside model prompts. Compare pooled and equal-family estimates; flag missing-family support rather than imputing accuracy. No historical selection allegation.
candidates.metric: Target θ is equal-family mean correctness over declared sealed reference items and two seeds. Report estimate−θ, family coverage and worst-family accuracy. One thousand showcase resamples quantify only conditional selection variability. Separately report reference-instance bootstrap and seed differences, conditional on these 12 families—not 1,000 independent model evaluations.
candidates.falsifier: Family-only bias attenuated by weighting while within-family bias persists supports the boundary. Persistent family-only bias weakens that account; small gaps across β favor population-specific robustness. Missing support, seed disagreement or wide intervals remain unresolved.
candidates.confound: Pilot ease may not transport. Reserve two untouched generator variants, 10 items each, for a separately labeled out-of-population check; report transport gaps without claiming two variants represent a universal family distribution.
candidates.feasibility: 760 confirmation/transport generations plus pilot ceiling 80; cheap conditional resampling. No uncertainty claim for unspecified task universes or historical selection. No run performed.
candidates.changes: Added random-to-strong selection, balanced contaminated showcases, disjoint ease predictors and sealed labels; defined the finite-population target and separated conditional, instance, seed and limited generator-transport uncertainty.

candidates.title: Overlap-aware evidence ledger with explicit abstention

sources.use: Separate recall-specific replications, broader paradigms and repeated samples.
sources.boundary: Failed recall replications and the favorable author-led pooled synthesis test different evidence units.

sources.use: Track alternate measurements and sample construction separately.
sources.boundary: Employment measurement disputes supply methods, not evidence about anomalous cognition.

candidates.mechanism: A global overlap graph joins reports sharing participants across any paradigm. Endpoint-specific estimates use connected components as dependence clusters; missing overlap produces conditional sensitivity intervals or abstention, not invented independent samples.
candidates.hypothesis: Overlap-aware uncertainty will improve synthetic interval coverage beyond paper-ID deduplication when reports share participants across paradigms.
candidates.experiment: Predeclare 500 seeds of 60 base samples yielding 180 reports in three paradigms: independent samples, exact duplicates, partial cross-paradigm overlap and correlated outcomes. Reveal the same report summaries and global hashed participant-set metadata to every method; hide generation parameters. Strip selected overlap metadata in a separate condition. Within each endpoint, equally weight base-sample summaries after removing exact report duplicates; bootstrap graph components 1,000 times for 95% intervals. Components spanning paradigms remain one cluster. With fewer than 20 components, refuse calibrated intervals. For missing edges, enumerate a fixed ten admissible overlap graphs and display the union of their intervals, explicitly conditional on this graph set. No cross-paradigm pooled effect is required.
candidates.baseline: Report pooling, paper-ID deduplication and global exact-sample deduplication receive identical inputs, endpoint labels, 1,000 resamples and output schema: estimate, interval, evidence scope, unresolved flag.
candidates.metric: Endpoint-specific 95% coverage with binomial Monte Carlo intervals; duplicate-count error; coverage conditional on declared overlap graphs; unresolved rate and retained precision.
candidates.falsifier: If exact-sample deduplication matches coverage and precision, prefer it. If conditional graph envelopes miss truth when the true graph is excluded, label that metadata case unresolved rather than claim robust coverage.
candidates.confound: Unknown dependence is not recoverable from labels alone; connected-component clustering can discard substantial information. Report over-connected graphs and honest abstention costs separately.
candidates.feasibility: Offline synthetic audit only; no real meta-analysis recomputed.
candidates.changes: Global participant identity now spans paradigms; dependence uses component bootstrap, matched output/resample budgets, explicit minimum cluster count, conditional missing-overlap bounds and Monte Carlo uncertainty.

candidates.title: Adjustment audit against ordinary randomized-trial practice

sources.use: Audit total assignment effects separately from proposed pathways.
sources.boundary: Original hormone/risk claims, larger replication and broader subjective-posture evidence remain separate.

sources.locator: DOI 10.1257/aer.100.2.573; Herndon–Ash–Pollin replication; Reinhart–Rogoff April 2013 response
sources.use: Separate association reconstruction from causal identification.
sources.boundary: An observational debt critique does not transfer its confounding structure to randomized posture assignment.

candidates.mechanism: A checker uses declared timing and estimands to reject unsupported pathway interpretations. Its value is measured against sound randomized-trial baselines, with unknown or misleading graph metadata tested explicitly rather than treating the simulator's hidden DAG as available evidence.
candidates.hypothesis: The checker may prevent interpretation errors beyond an ordinary trial analysis; added estimation accuracy is not presumed.
candidates.experiment: Freeze equations before sampling: A~Bernoulli(.5), X,U,e independent standard normal; M=aA+bX+U; H=tA+dM+cX+e. Null: a=t=d=0; subjective-only: a=.4,t=d=0; mediated: a=.4,d=.4,t=0. Collider case replaces M by .4A+U and H by cX+U+e. Report M and H separately; risk outcomes are outside this pilot. Across 1,000 datasets of 240 records per case, expose identical A,X,M,H tables and declared metadata; the checker never sees equations or hidden case IDs. Test correct, wrong and unknown metadata separately. Fit unadjusted H~A, baseline-adjusted H~A+X and indiscriminate H~A+X+M once per dataset; repeat for M. The checker selects among these cached fits or abstains: only verified pre-assignment covariates enter total-effect adjustment; unknown roles fall back to unadjusted estimates. Mediation remains unidentified without extra assumptions.
candidates.baseline: Unadjusted assignment and pre-assignment-X precision adjustment; all policies share six cached fits and identical output slots for total-effect estimate, interval and pathway-identification status.
candidates.metric: Bias and 95% HC3 interval coverage: H total=t+da and M total=a (collider H total=0), by endpoint and metadata regime; unsupported mediation assertions; precision and abstention costs. Hidden truth is used only by evaluation.
candidates.falsifier: If baseline-X practice matches error prevention and precision, prefer it. Wrong metadata that causes false pathway identification counts as failure; observational equivalence requires an unresolved pathway verdict, never automatic causal classification.
candidates.confound: Correct metadata is an assumption, not something observational tables validate. Random assignment identifies total effects under the simulated design, not mediator effects.
candidates.feasibility: Offline simulation; no human intervention or original-data reanalysis.
candidates.changes: Added strong precision-adjusted baseline, frozen structural equations, equal cached fits/outputs, blinded simulator truth, three metadata regimes and explicit unidentified mediation.

candidates.title: A crossed replication atlas with identifiable relative components

sources.use: Keep outcomes, measurement and intervention context separate.
sources.boundary: Broader subjective-posture synthesis and daily-life follow-up do not directly replicate original hormone/risk endpoints.

sources.use: Cross measurement with context to examine comparability.
sources.boundary: Policy-episode evidence supplies design lessons, not posture effects.

candidates.mechanism: Randomize treatment and instrument independently within each synthetic site. A crossed hierarchical model estimates relative site and instrument treatment contrasts; it abstains when interactions or weak site information prevent localization.
candidates.hypothesis: Crossing independent measurements will distinguish relative instrument bias from site moderation more reliably than confounding site and instrument.
candidates.experiment: For each endpoint separately generate Z=b_s+alpha_m+(tau+u_s+v_m+w_sm)A+epsilon, with independent participant noise and sum-to-zero u,v,w. Use 12 sites, 80 distinct participants per site, 20 in each treatment-by-instrument cell: 960 records and 960 genuinely independent measurements per endpoint. Predeclare site-only, instrument-only, both, neither and interaction stress scenarios; 200 seeds each. Fit site random intercept/slope plus fixed instrument and treatment interaction; use 1,000 whole-site bootstrap draws. Reserve four sites before tuning, retaining eight for fitting. Freeze contrasts and practical thresholds on a separate synthetic tuning seed set. Common absolute instrument bias is not identified; only relative components are estimands.
candidates.baseline: Confounded allocation uses the same 960 records, 960 independent measurements and treatment balance, assigning one instrument per site; harmonization uses one instrument everywhere. All output relative component intervals or 'not identifiable'; each gets identical fit/bootstrap budgets.
candidates.metric: Site-level 95% coverage; held-out-site endpoint prediction error; false localization and abstention. Label site-only or instrument-only only when its component interval clears the frozen threshold and the other's lies wholly within equivalence bounds; otherwise both/neither/unresolved. Report 25% four-class random guessing and always-unresolved baselines, scoring accuracy and abstention separately.
candidates.falsifier: If harmonization matches prediction and coverage, prefer it. If crossed intervals cannot localize components with eight training sites, report insufficient information. Large w_sm or equivalent models require unresolved localization, not a forced causal label.
candidates.confound: Sum-to-zero constraints identify relative contrasts, not physiological truth. Site and treatment-dependent instrument interactions can defeat decomposition; participant observations are never duplicated across instruments.
candidates.feasibility: Offline hierarchical simulation; no human replication or original-data reanalysis.
candidates.changes: Replaced paired recodings with independent randomized measurements; fixed equations/allocation, held-out sites, component estimands, cluster bootstrap, equal budgets and explicit interaction/weak-information abstention.

candidates.title: Locked confirmation with matched estimators and batch stress tests

sources.use: Freeze endpoint identity and multiplicity before confirmation.
sources.boundary: Hormone, risk and subjective endpoints remain distinct; the synthetic audit alleges no selective reporting by any original author.

sources.locator: arXiv 2303.12712v5, sections 1.1, 8 and 10
sources.use: Distinguish informative exploratory examples from calibrated confirmation.
sources.boundary: Selected demonstrations do not define a population success rate; this is not a replication of an early proprietary model.

candidates.mechanism: An append-only ledger freezes candidate contrasts and a family-wide selection rule. Independent confirmation estimates are compared with multiplicity-adjusted full-sample estimates under identical synthetic records, while secondary comparisons separate estimator precision from selection.
candidates.hypothesis: Held-out confirmation may reduce selected-effect inflation; any gain must survive budget matching and be reported alongside power costs.
candidates.experiment: Predeclare 300 campaigns per null, sparse and endpoint-specific signal scenario. Each has 30 synthetic standardized contrasts, ten per endpoint family, and 240 independent records split 120/120; every policy receives the same generated records. Freeze two-sided z tests with known unit variance and a family of all 30 contrasts. Split policy ranks first-half |z|, locks top three, then confirms each only if second-half p<=.05/3 with matching sign; effect estimate uses second half alone. Full-data comparator tests all 30 by Holm(.05) and reports the three largest-|z| estimates, clearly distinguishing selected from confirmed. Both compute all 30 contrasts on each half: exactly 60 evaluations; pooled sufficient statistics cost no extra contrast evaluations. Secondary comparison fixes the split-selected three and contrasts their 120-record held-out estimates with 120-record discovery estimates, isolating selection from sample size.
candidates.baseline: Holm full-data analysis plus unadjusted full-data selection; identical records, 60 evaluations and output fields. All retain every candidate and endpoint label, not only successes.
candidates.metric: Campaign-wise probability of any false confirmation; true-signal recovery; conditional selected-effect bias E[estimate-truth|selected], separately by endpoint; conditional confirmation power and estimator variance. Never compare only successful campaigns.
candidates.falsifier: If full-data Holm matches error control and improves recovery, prefer it. If reduced inflation vanishes at matched estimator sample size, credit precision/selection tradeoffs rather than the ledger. Shared-batch failure means confirmation is unresolved, not independently validated.
candidates.confound: Lock a second generator with correlated batch errors across halves before evaluation; retain nominal tests to expose miscalibration and report the failure. Administrative separation cannot create stochastic independence.
candidates.feasibility: Offline synthetic audit and ledger prototype; no participant research or model benchmark.
candidates.changes: Specified top-three selection, exact z tests, Holm/Bonferroni families, sign rule, estimator and bias estimand; matched records/evaluations, added sample-size-matched comparison and prelocked shared-batch stress.

candidates.title: Compare wage endpoints against a strong units-and-frame baseline

sources.locator: Card–Krueger original https://www.nber.org/papers/w4509; Neumark–Wascher comment https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1362; Card–Krueger reply https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.90.5.1397
sources.use: Keep survey, payroll and administrative employment constructions and sample frames separately identifiable.
sources.boundary: The reply remains attached to the challenge; no source is treated as establishing a universal wage effect.

sources.locator: Original endpoints https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20855902/; robustness study https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25810452/; endpoint-specific synthesis https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000356
sources.use: Transfer the requirement to distinguish physiological, behavioral and subjective endpoints into a ledger of distinct employment estimands.
sources.boundary: No posture effect size or evidence strength transfers to labor markets; distinguishing endpoints does not automatically reconcile estimates.

candidates.mechanism: A typed endpoint ledger checks numerator, denominator, period and establishment frame before comparing employment contrasts. A conventional units-and-frame table receives identical information. The test asks whether automatic compatibility checks add value beyond competent unit checking, without interpreting a descriptive contrast as a causal effect.
candidates.hypothesis: At equal information and analysis budgets, typed compatibility checks reduce false contradiction labels on incomparable endpoint/frame pairs while retaining genuine disagreement for aligned estimands; a competent plain table may perform equally well.
candidates.experiment: Preregister 40 synthetic state-pair episodes with 80 initial establishments per state, arranged in 10 independent global-shock regimes of four dependent episodes. Define headcount as all workers, weekly hours as total paid hours, FTE as hours/40 and survival as an open indicator. For initial-population means, closed establishments contribute zero to all four numerators and remain in the denominator; survivor means are separate estimands. Nonresponse remains missing, never zero. Generate survey/payroll/administrative-like extracts with overlap, composition shifts and systematic errors. Freeze exactly 24 analyses: 3 sources × 4 endpoints × 2 frames. Both workflows see identical records, formulas, units, frame notes and missingness flags. Lock pair comparisons and reporting rules before held-out simulation seeds. For each episode define truth as the full synthetic population descriptive difference in changes, not an identified causal effect. Use 2,000 regime-block bootstrap draws for uncertainty across episode contrasts; assess small-regime interval calibration by repeated simulated regimes.
candidates.baseline: A common-estimand table containing explicit formulas, units, dates, frame notes and all 24 results, with manual compatibility checks. Both workflows may output aligned agreement, aligned disagreement, incomparable or unresolved, and the same optional explanatory fields. No workflow is forced to assert a sign or causal conclusion.
candidates.metric: Primary: false contradiction labels / all predeclared truly incomparable pairs. Also report mismatch sensitivity and specificity; aligned sign errors / aligned nonzero-truth contrasts; unresolved fraction; and 95% regime-block interval coverage across repeated simulations. Define aligned disagreement as opposing nonzero descriptive contrasts only when numerator, denominator, period and frame match. Score numerics and compatibility separately; no causal-recovery score.
candidates.falsifier: If the typed ledger does not outperform the competent table on false contradictions while maintaining aligned-disagreement sensitivity, the simpler table is favored. Persistent disagreements after exact alignment count against endpoint mismatch as a sufficient explanation, without selecting a winner among the wage papers.
candidates.confound: Unobserved management shocks, strategic reporting and source-dependent missingness can leave aligned contrasts unresolved. Ten global-shock regimes may yield poorly calibrated bootstrap intervals; simulation coverage, not a nominal label, must reveal that limitation. No simulated result transports the episode to a universal wage law.
candidates.feasibility: A proposed offline generator, two deterministic report procedures and a fixed 24-result table; no original-data reanalysis or policy intervention has been executed.
candidates.changes: Replaced the weak one-column comparator with a competent formula/units/frame table and identical output choices. Defined four endpoint formulas, initial-population versus survivor denominators and closure versus nonresponse. Locked 24 analyses, separated descriptive compatibility from causal inference, and added global-regime sampling plus explicit metric denominators.

sources.locator: Original historical association https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.100.2.573; critical reconstruction https://peri.umass.edu/publication/does-high-public-debt-consistently-stifle-economic-growth-a-critique-of-reinhart-and-rogoff/; response https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rogoff/files/debt_growth_and_the_austerity_debate.pdf

candidates.mechanism: A frozen candidate-graph audit retains every structural world compatible with observed panel summaries. Time-direction placebos can remove some incompatible worlds, but exactly identical observational fixtures must remain underidentified. A strong residual-diagnostic baseline gets the same candidate families, data, fit budget and permissible conclusions.
candidates.hypothesis: Temporal placebos may reduce confidently wrong causal-direction declarations on distinguishable synthetic worlds; they must not create direction information in observationally equivalent or mixed-feedback worlds. Appropriate underidentification is a successful result, not an error.

Families include G_t=beta D_(t-1)+aG_(t-1)+u_t; D_t=gamma G_(t-1)+bD_(t-1)+v_t; both equations jointly; and latent persistent H_t entering both, with shared global shock Z_t. Generate 90 training and 90 held-out 50-country, 30-year panels using disjoint parameter regimes and shock processes. Add exact-equivalence fixtures by generating standardized correlated Gaussian observed arrays once and pairing them with forward and reverse structural factorizations having the identical observable distribution; hide construction labels. Both workflows fit the same four prespecified families with 10 fixed diagnostic operations. Freeze pseudocode: retain any family not rejected at a training-calibrated threshold; report a direction only when every retained family implies it, otherwise underidentified; empty retained sets mean model-misspecified/unresolved. The temporal workflow allocates diagnostics to time shifts/leads, the baseline to standard residual/serial-fit checks; publish both fixed menus before holdout. Calibrate only on training panels. Both use loss 1 for a wrong identified direction, 0.2 for abstention in identifiable fixtures, 0 for correct direction, and 0 for underidentified in exact-equivalence fixtures. Report each component separately so an arbitrary loss cannot hide overclaiming.

Report identified fraction, underidentification rate on exact-equivalence fixtures, missed mixed-feedback rate, retained-family coverage and global-shock-stratified calibration. Direction accuracy is scored only in preregistered distinguishable fixtures under the declared candidate family; simulator identity is not observational identifiability.

Any direction declaration on exactly identical forward/reverse fixtures is overclaiming. If the baseline matches calibration and useful identification coverage, its simpler diagnostic menu is favored. Zero identification everywhere does not establish improvement.

candidates.feasibility: All structural generators, decisions and losses would be frozen before the proposed offline benchmark. No economic causal analysis, paranormal test or original-data reanalysis has been executed.
candidates.changes: Specified observable inputs, structural families, retained-family decision pseudocode and common abstention losses. Added exactly identical observational fixtures, bidirectional effects, latent persistence and held-out global-shock regimes. Replaced country-only calibration with panel/global-shock-aware assessment and distinguished conditional identification from knowledge of simulator labels.
